archetypes.name: child-interface-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan describes precise argv flags, KV-output key names, FD-emission channel, and exit codes for roughly ten child scripts; any mismatch against those scripts' actual implementations will silently misparse output or pass wrong flags from step-7a.sh.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read each child script the plan lists as a dependency of step-7a.sh — generate-code-flow-diagram.sh, tracking-issue-summary.sh upsert-summary, rebase-checkpoint-probe.sh, flush-execution-issues.sh, capture-session-transcript.sh, append-tool-failure.sh, read-session-env-key.sh, larch-log.sh write and commit — or their sibling .md documentation files. For each one, compare the argv flag names, required-vs-optional parameter labels, KV output key names, and exit-code semantics the plan claims against what the script actually accepts and emits. Pay special attention to whether KV lines are emitted on FD 3 via lib-quiet emit_kv or on plain stdout, since step-7a.sh parses child output via command substitution and the channel determines whether the value is reachable. Flag every discrepancy between the plan's claimed interface and the real implementation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sanitizer-token-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan's comment-upsert-skip logic hinges on detecting a sanitizer-rejection token in generate-code-flow-diagram.sh's SKIP_REASON field, but the plan defers verification of the actual token to implementation time — if the real token does not match any of the fallback substrings the plan proposes, the skip gate will never fire.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/sanitize-mermaid-fragment.sh and skills/implement/scripts/generate-code-flow-diagram.sh (or their .md siblings) to identify the exact string that sanitize-mermaid-fragment.sh emits when it rejects a Mermaid fragment, and how generate-code-flow-diagram.sh propagates that string into its SKIP_REASON output field. Compare this against the plan's conservative-fallback heuristic of substring-matching the reject, rejected, or sanitiz tokens. Determine whether any rejection path emits a string that none of those substrings would match, or whether any non-rejection failure path coincidentally contains those substrings and would incorrectly suppress the comment upsert. The plan's test case 3 (diagram-rejected) stubs this path; verify that the stub's emitted SKIP_REASON value would actually trigger the skip gate under the plan's logic. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: flush-degraded-semantics
archetypes.rationale: The plan defines LOG_FLUSH_STATUS as degraded when flush-execution-issues.sh, capture-session-transcript.sh, or larch-log.sh commit fails but not for larch-log.sh write failures — this asymmetry must align with how existing SKILL.md prose and downstream steps interpret the KV to avoid silent data loss masquerading as an ok status.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the pre-bump flush body in skills/implement/SKILL.md (approximately lines 1457 to 1527) and identify every place a flush-phase helper failure is currently surfaced to the orchestrator: whether via explicit exit-code propagation, an append-tool-failure.sh call, or a logged warning only. Then compare this against the plan's LOG_FLUSH_STATUS aggregation rule, which sets degraded only for three specific helpers while treating all larch-log.sh write failures as best-effort writes that do not flip the status. Verify whether the plan's status-aggregation boundary matches the current SKILL.md operator-visible contract and whether any downstream step or Rebase Checkpoint Macro routing in SKILL.md consumes LOG_FLUSH_STATUS in a way that would misinterpret a best-effort-write failure swallowed into ok. Also check that the skipped-no-logs-commit enum value does not conflict with any no_logs_commit guard elsewhere in SKILL.md. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
